title: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated induction of large chromosomal inversions in human bronchial epithelial cells
protocol: Harvest HBECs as described in steps 9 (a–e) of the cell culture protocol for HBECs before transfection.
Count cells using a Neubauer glass chamber.
Seed approximately 8 × 10^4 cells in each well of a 6-well plate containing 2 ml keratinocyte medium to subsequently transfect the cells with gRNA/Cas9 expressing vectors.
Replenish keratinocyte medium two days after plating and perform double transfection with gRNA/Cas9 expressing vectors using FuGENE® HD Transfection Reagent.
Prepare a Transfection reagent: DNA mixture in a tube using a 4:1 FuGENE® HD Transfection Reagent to DNA ratio, then add the mixture in 200 μL Opti-MEM.
Resuspend by thorough pipetting and incubate for 15 min at 15°C–22°C.
Add the mixture dropwise in each transfection well containing 2 ml keratinocyte medium, in antibiotic- and serum-free conditions.
Trypsinize and collect HBECs as described in steps 9a–9d after transfection.
Wash collected HBECs once with 1× PBS.
Spin down the cells at 500 × g for 5 min at 15°C to 22°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL Opti-MEM or Keratinocyte medium and keep on ice until sorting.
Add DAPI into the transfected cell suspension at a final concentration of 500–1,000 ng/mL in 1× PBS.
Sort double-positive single cells expressing both GFP and mCherry using a flow cytometer (BD FACS Aria III).
Prepare 96-well plates by adding 100 μL keratinocyte medium supplemented with 1% Pen/Strep into each well to avoid contamination during FACS.
Sort one cell per well of the prepared 96-well plate.
Incubate single cell cultures undisturbed in humid 37°C/5% CO2 chamber for 7 days after FACS.
Add 100 μL antibiotic-free keratinocyte medium and start monitoring the clones under the microscope.

Replenish the medium every week by removing carefully the medium from each well using a pipette or multi-channel pipette without touching the bottom, and slowly adding 100 μL fresh Keratinocyte medium.
Once single cell-derived clones reach full confluency, commence the screening procedure.
Aspirate the medium from each well of the 96-well plates.
Wash once with 1× PBS.
Harvest cells derived from each well by adding 30 μL Trypsin/EDTA 1× and incubating for 5 min at 37°C.
Add an equal or larger volume of Trypsin Neutralizer Solution to the harvested cells.
Resuspend thoroughly by pipetting.
Transfer half of the amount of solution containing trypsinized cells into a new well of a 96-well plate.
Add 200 μL or more of keratinocyte medium to the transferred cell solution in the new well.
Directly add 30 μL of Quick Lysis Buffer to the cells which were not transferred.
Transfer the lysate from the untransferred cells into an Eppendorf tube.
Heat the lysate for 45 minutes at 60°C.
Heat the lysate for 10 minutes at 80°C for Proteinase K inactivation.
Use 4 μL of the lysate as template for PCR.
Store the remaining lysate at −20°C for up to 1–2 weeks or at −80°C for long-term storage.
Optimize PCR conditions for the set of primers used.
Use F1/R1 and F2/R2 primer combinations on wild-type genomic DNA template.
Run PCR reactions in a 1.3% agarose gel prepared with SYBR Safe DNA gel stain.
Identify clones yielding a PCR product at ∼770 bp and ∼1,300 bp for F1/F2 and R1/R2 respectively.
Run PCR reactions on the same clones using F1/R1 and F2/R2 primer combinations separately.
Amplification using these sets of primers reveals the presence of a wild-type allele in addition to the inverted one previously identified, indicating heterozygosity.
Purify PCR products using the QIAquick PCR Purification Kit.
Submit purified PCR products for Sanger sequencing using F1 or F2 primer for inverted breakpoint 1.
Use R1 or R2 primer for inverted breakpoint 2 in Sanger sequencing.
Transfer clones identified as "inverted" from each well of a 96-well plate to a well of a 24-well plate.
Further transfer cells to a well of a 12-well plate.
Expand cells to a well of a 6-well plate.
Transfer HBECs to larger wells only upon reaching confluency.
